review_content: The only thing that I know for sure has ended with the Marvel Cinematic Universe is my patience.
...a business play forcing us to make yet another down payment on our collective Marvel mortgage.
Be prepared to sweat, cry, and clench your armrest because Avengers: Infinity War is one hell of a ride.
If the Marvel Cinematic Universe aims to reshape popular entertainment, it needs to move beyond climax after climax with unremarkable, repetitive violence.
Watching Infinity War is like riding the most exhausting Six Flags roller coaster in existence three times consecutively

It's a little unwieldy, there are slow patches and the odd misstep, there are so many characters that your favourite might feel hard done by, and it is definitely Part 1... but the fact is that Infinity War is pretty damn thrilling.
The flavors of this multi-movie sundae blend beautifully.
Marvel betrays the richness of its comic books in pursuit of the bedazzlement of the modern blockbuster movie; leaving us undernourished but entertained.
If you've felt we're nearing superhero exhaustion, Marvel just went and changed the rules leaving you begging for more - proving yet again that they are the real masters of this game.

Somehow nearly every story that's been started in this cinematic universe gets serviced. That's no small feat for a series that centers on more than a dozen different characters, and yet still manages to make every one of them count.
This movie almost, but not quite seamlessly, brings together the disparate strands of a decade's worth of Marvel/Disney movies.
This is Marvel doing the absolute best version of the formula it's been criticised for overusing. They've blown it right up and now need to throw out that formula for good.
It's not exactly a crowded mess, but a tricky ending to this mad, mad, mad universe -- complete with all the requisite players -- will keep 'em coming back for more.
A celebration of mediocrity on a scale the cinema has never seen before. Avengers: Infinity War isn't a movie: it's advertising and brand management
Ten years ago this month, the Marvel universe was launched with the fresh, lively, relatively easygoing "Iron Man." It seems more like 100.
Maybe "Deadpool 2" will be better...
Never boring, visually impressive, but ultimately rather depressing and unsatisfying, Infinity War will leave you wanting more. But not necessarily in the best way.
It took us 19 movies over a span of 11 years to finally reach this destination. The end result? "Infinity War" is just too much of everything.
It's too much. Too many characters, too much action, too much everything. It's a superhero sur+ with too many heroes and not enough screen. It's Infinity overload.
Sitting through its 2 hours and 30 minutes is like gorging on tapas: You wind up both overstuffed and unsatisfied.
Even by Marvel's own standards of serviceable mediocrity, Infinity War fails.
Not even the threat of universal annihilation, it seems, will keep this assembly line from chugging ahead with its signature polished, mechanized efficiency.
There's no pacing in Avengers: Infinity War. It's all sensation and no pulse. Everything is big, all of the time.

Marvel's Avengers: Infinity War -- an overstuffed sausage of summer entertainment -- is the Ocean's Thirteen of spandexed heroism, if you can imagine a version of that movie with two times as many Brad Pitts and no poker dealers.
The noisy, bloated spectacles of combat were surely the most expensive parts of the movie, but the money seems less like an imaginative tool than a substitute for genuine imagination.
Throughout the film, rapidity of dialogue and drama is mistaken for actual rhythm, of which directors Anthony and Joe Russo have one mode: pedal-to-the-metal pandemonium.
Love or loathe the genre, when I see a film this ambitious actually hitting its targets AND managing to stay human and accessible, I can't help but be extraordinarily impressed.
The best Marvel film ever-the most complete, the most emotional, and the most thrilling.
An adrenaline rush of a film laced with bombastic action, thrilling setpieces and a level of satisfaction that's the cumulation of a decade-long journey.

Only now could the MCU arrive at a place where bluffs can be irrefutably called and gauntlets, real or metaphorical, can be thrown down. With audacity and thoughtfulness, "Infinity War" upends the comparative breeziness of all that came before it.
It's effective at being all the things it needs to be, even if that necessity is the thing that holds it back the most.
"Avengers: Infinity War" is almost three hours of non-stop action on multiple battlefields leading to a conclusion that will forever change the Marvel cinematic universe.
This movie isn't actually about the Avengers. It's about Thanos.

There is a fissure between critics and audiences, which I can admit. The movie is critic-proof. 'Avengers: Infinity War' is superhero porn, strictly for the fans, while 'Black Panther' was undeniably excellent, transcending the comic book fan base.
Infinity War is so gargantuan in scope, it almost becomes too much to digest. The smaller moments that have made the Marvel Cinematic Universe so enjoyable are lost in the spectacle.
The high doesn't last, but it's dizzying all the same.

AVENGERS: INFINITY WAR is nearly spread too thin by its massive amount of plot and characters. It redeems itself by being full of surprises and foreboding; focusing on the heroes' relationships and real peril in fierce, unrestrained action.

Expectations surpassed. An ambitious, exhilarating and deeply satisfying culmination to a decade of great Marvel films. Thanos now reigns as the best villain of the MCU. Period. [Full review in Spanish]

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: ...[Yan]'s written her own ticket here, confidently managing the shifting tones between each character's subplot and proving as adept at framing action as she is at mixing charming comedy with some truly discomforting horror elements.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey may not have the depth and darkness of the recent Joker but it is a fun popcorn flick.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey is a brutally satisifying and intoxicatingly vibrant explosion of fun. A film made by women for women about women, but operates in a capacity that is enjoyable for everyone.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: By letting action and comedy become augmentation for its underlying crime caper, it proves more character-driven romp a la Snatch than another ploddingly edgelord blockbuster.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: There's a pervasive air of desperation to this female-centric would-be comic-book action blockbuster, which flails about for nearly two hours trying to be edgy and snarky in 'Deadpool' mode but fails miserably on all counts.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Perhaps the greatest sign of female empowerment is that they can now fight, curse, maim, and kill as well as the boys do onscreen. I'm not sure what that says about our society, but it sure makes for some nasty fun at the Cineplex.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: A schizophrenic, barely comprehensible spinoff. It turns out Harley Quinn is entertaining only in small doses.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: As the opening installment of a projected franchise, it's pretty promising...

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: There's no denying the raucous, foul mouthed, glitter-bomb fun.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: An unholy and sadistic mess.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey may not amount to anything truly game-changing but it's still top-tier comic book stuff.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: A lean, tightly choreographed film, with gorgeous fight scenes.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: I came in hoping this would be a triumphant all-girl, kick-ass, riotous action movie. In the end I found it to be unfocused, derivative, loud, obnoxious, and actually kinda boring.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Combining all the ingredients that make comic book bros break out in hives, Birds of Prey is a candy-coloured curveball of a movie that doubles as a feminist fable and an apology for the poorly received Suicide Squad.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: A psychedelic piñata filled with more sweet than bitter things . [Full review in Spanish]

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey has all of the chaotic energy that a movie about Harley Quinn should have packaged in a frenetic action-filled romp that's impossible to resist. The best DCEU movie yet.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey isn't perfect, but it sure is fantabulous, and that's because Harley finally landed in the right hands: her own.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Violent and profane, but themes of teamwork, friendship.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey allows Robbie to truly let loose, giving her the space to develop an actual character beyond the one-dimensional, sociopathic quip machine that she was in Suicide Squad.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Led by a cutesy head-butt of a performance from superstar Margo Robbie, 'Birds of Prey' is a do-over of sorts for the much-maligned Suicide Squad.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: The result is a slapstick firework display of pleasantly cartoonish mayhem.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey puts the audience in the shoes (or roller skates) or somebody who gets a perverse thrill from nihilistic violence. Like it or not, it's a rush.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: It's too bad that things devolve into the ordinary by the last act, but until that happens, we zig and zag in often pleasant ways.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Perhaps not as fun as it wants to be, but the movie has high spirits and a refreshing perspective that goes a bit deeper than just grrrl power.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: The toxic male gaze of Suicide Squad is thankfully absent, but the sloppy writing and shoddy filmmaking remain intact.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey make mincemeat of anyone in their way.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: As vibrant and colorful as a pyrotechnic spectacle. Margot Robbie commands this emancipation story with charm, strength and confidence. [Full Review in Spanish]

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Birds of Prey has a shaky start, gets a bit too infatuated with its own kitschy conceits, but when it settles in to the characters quieter stories and the main action, it nails it.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: Harley keeps her ruthless "devil may care" iconic status but she is not in the same movie as the Birds of Prey.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: In spite of the formulaic constraints of the male-dominated genre, BIRDS OF PREY soars, swoops, glides, dive-bombs, and sings.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: It's passable entertainment on the superhero level, but another opportunity missed to revel in the zany gleeful madness of Harley.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
review_content: The type of scrappy mayhem that gives a sparkle of excitement to the mostly bland and boring DCEU.

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

movie_title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)

Due in no small part to the daily horrors of the Trump presidency, Lee seems to have recaptured that spark that gave us the kind of scathingly frank commentary coupled with an intimate African American perspective invocative of Do the Right Thing
John David Washington is... an up-and-coming talent worth keeping an eye on.
BlacKkKlansman is a story of bravery, audaciousness, hypocrisy, and history -- all pulled together in something that feels horribly, inescapably current.

BlacKkKlansman is a film with a great cast, but the way director Spike Lee decided to force his message makes the movie feel heavy-handed and oddly redundant in parts.
The great revelation of Spike Lee's BlacKkKlansman is how imagery can be used as powerful motivators, cultivating the way people feel and act.
The film's central concerns - hateful rhetoric dressed up as "pride," prejudiced cops abusing their power - feel viscerally relevant.
Lee's joint is undoubtedly a raging inferno of all too relevant social commentary. It's a powerhouse spine-tingler which proactively manages to kick racism in the balls at brute force.
It's frighteningly timely and timeless, yes, but Lee knows how to approach it like a comedy that stands on its middle fingers. Power to the people indeed.
BlacKkKlansman is Spike Lee's most significant film since Do The Right Thing and Malcolm X.
The chemistry between Washington and Driver is essential to maintaining the rythm of the film persistent and entertaining in a constant shift between crime and comedy. [Full review in Spanish]

Ten years ago, during our optimistic delusions of a post-racial America, we might have naively called such a movie over-the-top. But arriving the same week as an actual white-nationalist rally on the National Mall, it's horrifically spot-on.

Haunting, humorous, and thought provoking in equal measure.

review_content: A rather remarkable sequel.
Rami Malek as Freddie Mercury gives a transformative performance.

If, indeed, the intent of this bio-pic is to chronicle the events that led to Queen and Freddie Mercury's legendary performance at Live Aid, well, I guess the goal has been met. The movie, as it is, is fine. But it could have been so much more.
"Bohemian Rhapsody" the song is a sonic masterpiece and "Bohemian Rhapsody" the movie is just a conventional rock flick, one all too ordinary for a man and a band that exemplified the extraordinary.
I really can't say enough about Rami Malek ... He's why this movie works as well as it does.

[It] doesn't feel like a con job; rather, it's a genuine attempt to bring Queen and the legacy of Freddie Mercury to life on the big screen for the one thing that reigned supreme in their dynasty: the music. And what music it is.
It's a kind of magic any way you slice it.
It is a wig-and-teeth movie, but Malek's performance really sells the entire performance.

In common with The Proclaimers film, this is very much a jukebox musical which rests entirely on the viewer's tolerance (or love) for Queen's music -- don't like the band; nothing to see here -- and Rami Malek's appropriately majestic performance.
I enjoyed it, but this isn't much real life, it's more fantasy.
While flawed, much like the band's music, this is a film that is very easy to sit back and enjoy, even if you can appreciate that, at times, it's not particularly very good.
What we ultimately wanted from Bohemian Rhapsody was not carbon-copied concerts, but behind-closed-doors insight into a deeply private, complicated, internationally beloved superstar.

Like a lot of depictions of rock music on film, Bohemian Rhapsody lacks both the stylistic daring of a music video and the outright euphoria of a proper musical, but it gets closer to both with the Live Aid sequence.

The critical failure of Bohemian Rhapsody is that, 134 minutes after the lights go down, the members of Queen just seem like four blokes who've been processed through the rusty machinery of a Hollywood biopic.
In hindsight, it would be better if this movie didn't exist at all.
A bolder film might have explored the relationship between Mercury's hedonism, his mostly closeted sexuality and his on and off-stage personas in a more nuanced way.
Malek's Freddie is a musical performance for the ages, but the film he's trapped in is the three-minute radio edit that the character and real songwriter would have never settled for.
Although Malek looks the part, and has Freddie's dance moves down, his performance is all stiff British accent and overbite.
Despite its intentions to get close to Mercury, Bohemian Rhapsody is as intimate as a sold-out stadium show, with none of the accompanying power.
What's arrived at the other side of this troubled production history is a work that's all spirit, no soul.
The songs are where the movie really gets its emotional core, and that alone is perhaps worth the ticket of admission.
Fortunately, the film comes to life any time that Queen take to the stage, thanks to dynamic staging and dedicated performances from all four stars.
The film has a secret weapon: Rami Malek. As Mercury he is spectacular.
This will rock you.
The final hurrah for Mercury's genius, this huge, hubristic spectacle lets you grant his troubled film a pass: at least it keeps on fighting to the end.

An object example of how a film can be entertaining and even exhilarating without being particularly good, Bohemian Rhapsody has the driving energy of a stadium anthem and the fizzy meaninglessness of a bubblegum pop song.
I'm happy to report that this is not Bohemian Crapsody.

Frankly, if you are not cheering along with the crowd as Mercury belts out an ultra-satisfying rendition of "We are the Champions," then a doctor should check your pulse. Somewhere, an outrageous artist knows that his Queen movie rules.
Bohemian Rhapsody might not be the be-all end-all story of Freddie Mercury and Queen ... but it's easily the next best thing.

First Man doesn't just dwell on its subject's achievements. It takes a beat to glance into Armstrong's personal motivations and vulnerabilities while using technical mastery to tell an engrossing true-life story.

It's no wonder that [Damien] Chazelle loves portraying obsessed men because he is clearly obsessed with the details. He pays attention to everything. From the smallest bolt holding a ship together to the tempo of Justin Hurwitz's fabulous score.
In the end, Chazelle manages to fashion First Man into a gripping account of one of mankind's greatest achievements. The only slight frustration is the stoic-to-a-fault central character.
For all its technical merits, narrative intrigue, and fine acting, something feels hollow.
This may be [Damien] Chazelle's best film yet. It may not be a joyous celebration, but watching the intense performances and the meticulous detail, should put your over the moon.
"First Man" soars as much when it's staying grounded as it does when Armstrong and the dreams of the nation finally reach that far-off star.
Chazelle demonstrates the rare skill of staging epic spectacles within a most intimate setting.
The up-close, frantic camera shots are replaced by glorious wide shots of the Saturn V rocket lifting off and leaving the Earth's atmosphere, accented by Justin Hurwitz's beautiful score.

There are flashes of brilliance in First Man, but like the stuck thruster that almost killed Neil Armstrong before he ever got to the moon, the shoddy photography sends the whole thing spinning out of control.
Damien Chazelle is an enthusiastic, visually expressive filmmaker with practically nothing of interest to say about the human experience.
[Chazelle] offers a fresh perspective on Neil Armstrong's life at work, detailing his journey as an astronaut on a mission mostly shot either from an intimate or first-person point-of-view.

A film that doesn't glorify Neil Armstrong as a national hero, but rather opts to illustrate the determination of a hermetic and introspective person who silently mourns the mourning caused by a family impairment. [Full review in Spanish]
This Neil Armstrong biopic excels at the kinetic launches and spaceflight sequences, but drags along when it has both feet on the ground.
One of the most compelling and inherently dramatic works of the year.
A great film about loneliness, mourning and the human ability of achieving incredible things. [Full review in Spanish]

I have no idea what compels a person to get inside of a tiny metal compartment and get blasted off into the sky ... But oh, Chazelle and his team do an incredible job of giving us a hint of what that rush must feel like.
The delayed gratification makes the ending all the more thrilling.
A sobering study of grief and obsession delivered with a stunning eye of respect for Armstrong. Chazelle launches his excellence in filmmaking into the cosmos.
First Man captures that longing for safety quite well, treating it as a myth that's essentially supernatural in its elusiveness.
Trends downwards from its thrilling opening sequence.
First Man, although concerned with a world-historic, world-changing event, has a limited goal and framework...
An undeniably solid and occasionally spectacular big screen depiction of an achievement that still has the power to grip the world 50 years after it happened.

Combining breathtaking, claustrophobic cabin sequences that feel like you're being shot into space in a shoebox, with Ryan Gosling's restrained-but-pained performance as Neil Armstrong, a grieving father focused on the mission, it's a powerhouse.

Chazelle has done it again, delivering one of the finest space films ever made by focusing on the everyday humanism of our reluctant heroes rather than flag-waving cliches, thus cementing his place on the forefront of the next frontier of cinema.

Joaquin Phoenix kills it in dark, timely DC origin movie that is no laughing matter. Will he be second Joker to win an Oscar?
This is a truly nightmarish vision of late-era capitalism - arguably the best social horror film since Get Out - and Joaquin Phoenix is magnetic in it.

If you strip the Joker and his nearly 80-year history as a cultural icon out of this film, as well as all the 1970s movie homages, there's not a whole lot left except for Phoenix's performance, and it's the kind of turn that's destined to be divisive.
This is the world post-Joker and with nothing but shaky-breathed respect for the filmmaking and storytelling achievement it represents, God help us all.
Todd Phillips delivered a game changing comic book film, and I cannot wait to see it again.
It's chilling and ironically, still a fun way to spend two-hours escaping into a fictional world. Joker is such a great film that ventures away from the comic books and dives more into reality.

Whether Joker is a social commentary on issues such as poverty or mental illness, a new mysterious take on the best known DC Comics villain, or another unforgettable piece of cinema by Martin Scorsese, you'll need to see to believe it.
Joker is one of the true masterpieces of the superhero cinema, and one of 2019's greatest achievements.
Joker is a solid, well-made film that, ultimately, has a bit of an identity crisis.

Having brazenly plundered the films of Scorsese, Phillips fashions stolen ingredients into something new, so that what began as a gleeful cosplay session turns progressively more dangerous - and somehow more relevant, too.
Phoenix has plumbed depths so deep and given such a complex, brutal and physically transformative performance, it would be no surprise to see him take home a statuette or two come award season.
What do you get when you take a poor, mentally unstable loner and you treat him like trash? The answer given in Todd Phillips's ingenious new feature is Batman's arch nemesis, the Joker.

Joker succeeds thanks to the talents of Phoenix, who's crafted a layered, terror-inducing antagonist, and earned his rightful place alongside Heath Ledger and Jack Nicholson in the pantheon of all-time-great Jokers.
Nobody who sees this new film will ever need any other version.
Phillips may want us to think he's giving us a movie all about the emptiness of our culture, but really, he's just offering a prime example of it.
As social commentary, Joker is pernicious garbage.
Feeble posturing, asinine pop psychology and political analysis charged with all the cynicism of a mollycoddled teen dropout in fake Oakleys and a home customised Linkin Park tee.

Superhero blockbuster this is not: a playful fireman's-pole-based homage to the old Batman television series is one of a very few lighthearted moments in an otherwise oppressively downbeat and reality-grounded urban thriller...
Bold, devastating and utterly beautiful, Todd Phillips and Joaquin Phoenix have not just reimagined one of the most iconic villains in cinema history, but reimagined the comic book movie itself.
I've not always gotten along with Phoenix's mannered, muscle-strained approach to his craft, but here he makes a compelling case for going full-tilt.
"Joker" is a dark, brooding and psychologically plausible origin story, a vision of cartoon sociopathy made flesh.

Joaquin Phoenix's fully committed performance and Todd Phillips' masterful albeit loose reinvention of the DC source material make Joker a film that should leave comic book fans and non-fans alike disturbed and moved in all the right ways.
More character study than comic book movie, and anchored by an Oscar-worthy Joaquin Phoenix, Joker is a bravura blockbuster that proves you don't need superpowered scraps to dazzle.

Simply calling Joker a "comic book movie" does it a disservice; it is a story that feels like it could be about any number of disaffected people who are marginalized by the ruthless world in which we live.

Rango is the most beautiful animated film since the golden age of hand-drawn cartoons. Shame that the movie has no heart beneath all that beauty, though.

review_content: ...probably a little too generic (and long) to win over a grown-up audience rendered blasé about movie robots by the Transformers movies, but kids should respond well to its finely calibrated wish-fulfilment story.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: It's all very heavy-handed, but maybe kids of about ten to thirteen will be more taken with it.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The robot has the heart and the human has to learn to feel again in this unabashedly cheesy but irresistible fairy tale.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel is a movie of simple ideas and even simpler pleasures.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: It should be disastrous. It should suck on Wonder Bread with a side order of Craptastic to wash it down. And yet... and yet... my God, is there actually a good time in there?

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: I didn't care which robot won the fight. And I didn't care about the people either.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Mostly it's dopey. The movie just begs too many logical questions for its own good.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel is what happens when people who know nothing about science fiction make a science fiction movie.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel works so well and the concept is so obvious -- what kid out there hasn't wanted their own robot? that it's surprising Hollywood hasn't made Robo Rocky before.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Though the premise of fighting robots does seem a plausible and intriguing extension of the contemporary WWE world, Real Steel is hampered by leaden, clichéd moments in which a stubborn boy teaches his childish father a valuable lesson.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel is ridiculous, but it is not dispiriting. If you're going to make this movie, it should be made just this way, with commitment, verve and a complete disregard for physics, robotics and environmentalism.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Every cliché from sports movies, underdog stories and father-son dramas is trotted out and played with a straight face.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: There's really no excuse

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The reason we ARE here to see "Real Steel" is the rockin' robots. The deft use of CGI, motion capture and animatronics makes the action look real and believable (in a bombastic Hollywood way).

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel should not work on any level, but it succeeds on many, thanks to its appealing, unpretentious and deceptively involving approach to its tale.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: It's probably the best cliched father-connects-with-the-son-he-never-knew with boxing robots movie you're likely to see.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Even if the story in "Real Steel" isn't new, it is a crowd-pleaser, told with humor and pace. And those distinctive robots are the real deal.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The tear-jerking in Real Steel is as shameless as its product placement. We're being hustled.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: A science-fiction family film in which nine-foot-tall boxing robots are greased not with oil but with schmaltz.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Lovers of blood sport action ... are going to enjoy the well-staged fighting sequences ... while tender hearts seeking emotional depth will find the father-son conflict reasonably engaging.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Most viewers over the age of 12 will feel they have stepped into a confused, unambitious piece of futurama weighed down by Shawn Levy's uninspired and limp direction.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: An old-fashioned potboiler made up of cinematic spare parts [that] work[s] in a crass, manipulative way. But...anybody without a bleeding heart will probably be giggling rather than cheering by the final fade-out.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Neither as bad as it sounds nor quite as good as it could be, although the 9-year-old bruiser next to me pummeled the armrest, spilled his soda and screamed "awesome" through every one of the fight scenes.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Yes, it's unapologetically sentimental (and sometimes unapologetically cheesy), but Shawn Levy's film has an irresistible force.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The movie uses every trick it can to pull this off, which means using us. But to paraphrase Bill Withers, I want to spread the news that if it feels this good getting used, then keep on using me until you use me up.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: "Real Steel" turns out to be less toxic than you'd expect, if you take it as a family picture aimed at boys, which it is, and grant that boys have an endless appetite for robot smashing, which they do.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: A Frankenstein-like compendium of fight movies haphazardly bolted together in the hope that something will spark to life.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: unsteadily teeters on the brink of unmitigated disaster for over two hours of metal-clanging robo-fighting and teary-eyed human melodrama

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel may have a hardened outer shell, but it's pure marshmallow on the inside.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: At least the depressingly similar Transformers franchise serves up its soullessness with a side order of crazy. Real Steel just piles on the schmaltz.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: [It's] a big, expensive-looking entertainment masquerading as a modest, straightforward one, and sometimes the illusion works.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: [Real Steel] is the undercard you're forced to sit through in order to get to the real main event, which, in this case, just never materializes.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: ROCKY with Robots? You betcha, and it works!

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Kudos to Shawn Levy, he's made a movie many of us didn't expect - the personification of what a Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots movie should be.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: I suspect a lot of what I found synthetic and sort of galling in "Real Steel" will work just fine with the target audience.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Even in its fist-pumping finale Disney's economic parable remains pessimistic: America wins the popularity contest, but the Asians win the purse.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel falls somewhere near the intersection of elation and shame, essentially reworking the Sylvester Stallone arm-wrestling non-classic Over The Top for the equally ridiculous sport of android fisticuffs, and mostly getting away with it.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Imagine what you'd get if you squished "Rocky" and "WALL-E" together in a giant industrial press: a gooey, drippy mess, leaking lubricant and metal shards all over the factory floor.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: "Real Steel" is a real movie. It has characters, it matters who they are, it makes sense of its action, it has a compelling plot. This is the sort of movie, I suspect, young viewers went to the "Transformers" movies looking for.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Director Shawn Levy is a certified lightweight who always goes for the easiest emotional payoff. But Hugh Jackman's lovable as a loser, Dakota Goyo has spunk and charm, and the robot battles are genuinely thrilling.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Real Steel? As opposed to what, imitation metallic substitute? Giant beams made of cheese?

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Pure programming from the opening frame, hitting artificial beats throughout, using the shiny robots to distract from painfully leaden filmmaking. It's not Rocky, it's just wrecked.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: A well made but instantly forgettable robot-boxing movie that dishes out clichés blow-by-blow for its 12-year-old-boy target audience.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Every moment is prettified as if this were some sort of prestige project; there isn't an image shot plainly if it couldn't be reflected in a puddle.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: This thing is tons of fun to watch and kids ages 10 to 15 are going to love it.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Adding giant robots to your typical sentimental underdog sports story doesn't make the sappiness any more palatable, just way more expensive to produce.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Thanks to an admittedly corny script, some amazing fight scenes, and a terrific cast, "Real Steel's" actually a winner by split decision.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The film serves a broad audience without exploiting the classic boxing tradition. "Mind over matter" may be age-old, but this one delivers it in a fun package.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: a pretty solid mix of an underdog fighting movie and a movie about a father and son. And all of it is set against the backdrop of some wicked-cool robots fighting.

review_content: Just plain unpleasant to sit through. So much of the movie is spent amid screaming crowds and abrasive music, often in dark, trashy dives.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Surely a story as elementary and essentially derivative as this one could be told in less than 127 minutes.

review_content: Some audiences will enjoy the film for what it is; they will bob and weave with fun robot fight scenes. But I found little here that is truly inspiring.

review_content: Channeling Spielberg...as well as dozens of Popcorn King imitators, (the director) winds up delivering a braindead blockbuster that is guaranteed to generate income, if not entertainment.

review_content: Aas the plot proceeds from boy-meets-dad verbal sparring to an uneasy peace to the underdog-vs.- champion title bout, it becomes increasingly easy to forgive its many nicks.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Quite cheesy, yet exhilarating and mindlessly entertaining. It's a fun, crowd-pleasing popcorn movie that will leave you hungry for a sequel. Child star Dakota Goyo has a very bright future ahead of him.

review_content: Is Real Steel original, amazingly directed, acted wonderfully or something you've never seen? No. Is it fun? Definitely.

review_content: The result is predictable but enjoyable. And the robot fights are cool, and infrequent enough that we don't get sick of them.

It depicts Edward Snowden's ethical dilemmas in a political vacuum that disregards America's increasingly complex security threats.
The film would have been better served by a healthy degree of Oliver Stone's characteristic urgency and outrage.
Stone has made a film aimed at breaking out Snowden's story to the masses but it's made with such limpness that a swift read of his Wikipedia page will prove far more exciting.

Stone's exile in the desert of overheated irrelevance has now ended. "Snowden" isn't just the director's most exciting work since "Nixon" (1995) - it's the most important and galvanizing political drama by an American filmmaker in years.

Son of Saul is one hell of a debut, with the emphasis on hell: it's set entirely, and with pitiless, unyielding intensity, inside Auschwitz-Birkenau.
What elevates Son of Saul is that first-time feature filmmaker Laszlo Nemes has constructed a new way of grasping the insanity and senselessness of those long-ago crimes.
Nemes' ability to inject the material of a concentration camp survival story with bracing cinematic energy is all the more impressive because it's the writer-director's first feature.
The tight focus on one character to the exclusion of everything else can be exhausting to the viewer, but it never comes across as just a gimmick; it's too central to the story Nemes is telling.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

review_content: A spectacular, full-throttle joyride of thrills, exhilarating, screen-filling visuals, emotional heft and humor, with familiar characters and new faces we'll almost certainly be seeing again.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Fans can expect plenty of surprises and awe-inspiring visual wizardry.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: Everything a fan could want from a Star Wars film and then some.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The Last Jedi is a top-of-the-line, A-+ Star Wars and scifi movie -- one that we'll be watching and discussing for as long as there's a galaxy far, far away.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The movie suffers a little from uneven pacing and occasionally lost my focus here and there but it is a worthy addition to the canon.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: It took them 40 years, but they've finally done it. The best Star Wars film of the series. There. That's it. It's that simple.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy
review_content: The future of the galaxy has never been in safer hands.

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

genres: Action & Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction & Fantasy

Now, with his fourth film McQueen turns in another 180 type maneuver. Widows sees three women, who are all left widows when their criminal husbands are killed, with nothing in common coming together to do something no one would have expected of them.
There can be power in kindness and in camaraderie alongside crime and corruption, and that is the nuance, the depth, and the politics Widows provides.

Ultimately "Widows" is terrific on its face as a crime thriller. It's violent, it's kinetic and it's beyond watchable. But if you want to pay a bit more attention...there's so much more happening under the surface.
A thriller for modern women who identify more with the messiness of human lives than with flattened slogans about how great women, as a monolithic group, are.
The killer heist film Widows is both burial and rebirth, a cool caper peppered with vivid characters, high stakes, sharp plot points and jagged reversals.
Davis' stoicism has been her stock in trade for years. That whip-smart personality of forceful vengeance makes her the ideal woman to head this stellar cast of actors.

Never afraid to sink her teeth into a role, Davis crafts a tough-as-nails exterior for Veronica, snarling insults at the other women while trying to mask the creeping sense of dread that continues to mount as the deadline draws near.
Obviously this isn't meant to be an Ocean's-style caper, but the glacial pace might leave you wanting a bit more heist and a bit less ice.
Widows is a film that has it all - a smart script, driving crime thriller energy, memorable characters and something to say about the world we live in.
This is thrilling, handsomely-paced filmmaking that proves there are no boundaries when tackling a genre film
Widows is one of the best movies of the year, featuring dynamic performances, great twists, and a fascinating story.
This is a high-octane adrenaline ride and if the comedown is a bit too sharp to be wholly comforting, watching it again to feel the thrills of its highest moment feels like the best remedy.
Thrilling and suspenseful with action performed by an all-star cast.
The violence is quick, brutal, and never quite what we expect. McQueen is more interested in the consequences of that violence, and the consequences are never pretty.

High-profile actors performing in a non-sequel that explores rich themes of grief, betrayal and onerous family legacies is just increasingly rare. Widows may overreach a bit, but who can be mad at the effort?
Viola Davis says more with her inner smoulder than many actors manage with the proverbial thousand words.
Davis is masterful as the strong leader of this resilient group of women and Rodriguez and Debicki match her in every scene.
The plotting is also clunky at times and not much of the action is plausible, but with these astonishing performances, the flaws almost don't matter.
Widows boast the best cast of the year and is sure to be that rare film that bridges the gap between arthouse and mainstream.
As much about class, race, politics, and privilege as it is about heists, Widows presents a fallen world where thievery is just part of life.
Every day, women are robbed of respect, independence and opportunity... but Steve McQueen's thriller satisfyingly shows them taking it back.
Seeing these actresses work together turns the heist caper genre on its head and provides one more reason why this year is the year of the woman.

[T]his genre piece is much more than most of its pulpy brethren showing up in movie theaters and it's refreshing to see such vivid characters, as well as such stinging commentary on racism and sexism on display in a thriller.

Widows is an exciting and suspenseful heist thriller that proves itself to be about much more than just the heist itself. It's a stinging social commentary on modern-day America that is backed by powerful performances.
Widows is uncompromising, visceral and surprisingly thought-provoking.
A heist movie elevated by layers of empathy and complexity.
Podcast review
McQueen's version of 'Widows' offer more than a straightforward heist film. There are dirty politics and family struggles being played out.
McQueen sets a relentlessly portentous tone and employs lots of stark mise-en-scene, but all the fuss feels arbitrary here - the pulpy story simply doesn't warrant such grave stylization.
Everything about Widows works. There's just no resisting it.

While the sound and fury produced a robust response... the end result felt to me like a second-rate Elmore Leonard crime caper, a little too fanciful to be either top-drawer drama or stirring feminist tale.
It is a gloomy, violent film, but it can also be boring. There are excesses that inevitably take their toll. [Full review in Spanish]
An incredibly well-made, taut and realistic heist thriller. It's not a fun romp the way the Ocean's series, and others cut from that cloth, tend to be. This is a brutal film that pulls no punches.
I hesitate not a whit in calling Widows the most satisfying heist film of the year.
It's a genuine pleasure watching all of these talents work together in various combinations, moving through this layered, well-structured story. Widows is easily one of the best films of the year.
The cast makes up for most of the missing pieces.
The heist itself isn't all that clever, but the way the plot slowly unfurls is both brainy and emotionally intense.
Gritty and ferocious, McQueen has you rooting for these ladies from the get-go, you feel invested in the story from the very beginning.
Widows is an instant crime classic.
Widows does a generally decent job at keeping its pace up for most of the film, but it can be occasionally dispiriting for some of its meatier themes to fall by the wayside.

McQueen plays gleefully with all the genre's tropes, from double crosses to training montages, subtly rewiring the interpersonal relationships and motivations, all while two of the women juggle childcare.

It's a rare experience when you watch a film that you didn't want to end, and it's not every day where I call out something that merits five stars. But this is a five-star film, continuing McQueen's outstanding record in filmmaking.

"Widows" resembles an urban expose like "The Wire" more than a caper romp like "Ocean's 8." It's much tougher, grittier, literally a matter of life and death. Tone is everything in a movie and, in this one, McQueen sticks to it brilliantly.
A pitch-perfect demonstration of an auteurist director demonstrating his singular vision in a more mainstream canvas.
Yet if the story's political, racial and gender subtext sometimes acts as a drag on the action, it gives the film a depth and richness other films of the genre often lack.
